stops.title: Rutherford model & Bohr's atomic model
stops.inShort: Bohr's postulates: quantized angular momentum L = nh/(2π); radiation emitted/absorbed when jumping between stationary orbits: hν = E_i − E_f. Radius r_n ∝ n²/Z; velocity v_n ∝ Z/n; energy E_n = −13.6 Z²/n² eV.

stops.title: Hydrogen spectrum & de Broglie's explanation
stops.inShort: Rydberg formula: 1/λ = R (1/n_f² − 1/n_i²), R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹. Series: Lyman (UV, n_f=1), Balmer (Visible, n_f=2), Paschen (IR, n_f=3). Standing electron waves: 2π r_n = n λ.

stops.title: Nuclear size, mass defect, binding energy & radioactivity
stops.inShort: Nuclear radius R = R₀ A^(1/3) (R₀ ≈ 1.2 fm). Binding energy ΔE_b = Δm c². Law of radioactive decay: N = N₀ e^(−λt); half-life T_½ = 0.693/λ; activity A = λN (1 Bq = 1 decay/s).

board.text: Derive an expression for law of radioactive decay. Define one becquerel (Bq).
board.answer:
By the law of radioactive decay, the rate of decay (−dN/dt) at any instant is directly proportional to the number of undecayed nuclei N present at that instant:
−dN/dt = λ N ⇒ dN/N = −λ dt.
Integrating from t = 0 (N = N₀) to t (N = N): ln(N/N₀) = −λt ⇒ N = N₀ e^(−λt).
One becquerel (1 Bq): Activity of a radioactive sample is 1 Bq if 1 nucleus decays per second.

points.text: Definition of 1 Bq = 1 decay per second

board.text: An electron in hydrogen atom stays in its second orbit for 10⁻⁸ s. How many revolutions will it make around the nucleus in that time? [e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg, ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C²/Nm², h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s]
board.answer:
For n = 2 in H-atom: r₂ = 4 r₁ = 4 × 0.53 × 10⁻¹⁰ m = 2.12 × 10⁻¹⁰ m.
v₂ = v₁ / 2 = 2.18 × 10⁶ / 2 = 1.09 × 10⁶ m/s.
Time period T₂ = 2π r₂ / v₂ = (2 × 3.142 × 2.12 × 10⁻¹⁰) / (1.09 × 10⁶) = 1.222 × 10⁻¹⁵ s.
Number of revolutions N = t / T₂ = 10⁻⁸ / (1.222 × 10⁻¹⁵) ≈ 8.18 × 10⁶ revolutions.

board.text: Disintegration rate of a radio-active sample is 10¹⁰ per hour at 20 hours from the start. It reduces to 5 × 10⁹ per hour after 30 hours. Calculate the decay constant.
board.answer:
Activity A₁ = 10¹⁰ /hr at t₁ = 20 hr; A₂ = 5 × 10⁹ /hr at t₂ = 30 hr.
Since A₂ = A₁ / 2, the half-life T_½ = t₂ − t₁ = 30 − 20 = 10 hours.
Decay constant λ = 0.693 / T_½ = 0.693 / 10 = 0.0693 hr⁻¹ (or 1.925 × 10⁻⁵ s⁻¹).
